findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction changed `displayView: .readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC handleDisplayActions maps `.readerModeLongPressAction` to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which saves the page to the reading list, while `.readerMode` (the only caller of `toggleReaderMode()`) is now never produced. Tapping the toolbar reader-mode button, VoiceOver magic tap, or summarizer long-press (all dispatch showReaderMode) no longer enters or exits reader view; instead it adds a reading-list entry and shows a toast. Fix: restore `displayView: .readerMode`.
findings.failureMode: User taps reader-mode button on an article → page is added to reading list instead of opening reader view; reader mode cannot be toggled.
findings.title: showReaderMode now maps to readerModeLongPressAction (adds to reading list)

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry swapped the branches: `.available` now yields false and every other state true, contradicting the retained comment "will be enabled after action gets executed". Tapping the button to open reader view records enabled=false and closing it records enabled=true, corrupting toolbar.reader_mode_button_tapped data. It also breaks the unchanged testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes: default readerModeState is nil → isEnabled=true, and because ToolbarTelemetry passes it into the isPrivate extra, `XCTAssertEqual(savedExtras.isPrivate, false)` fails. Fix: restore `.available: true`, `default: false`.
findings.failureMode: Opening reader view logs enabled=false (and vice versa); existing ToolbarMiddleware reader-mode test fails.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry `enabled` value inverted

findings.description: Condition changed from `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL` to `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`. Reader-mode URLs are `http://localhost:<port>/reader-mode/page?url=...`, so isWebPage() is already true; base nil'd them so AddressBarState kept the decoded `displayURL` set by BVC. Now the raw internal URL is dispatched with cancelEdit and AddressBarState stores it (`toolbarAction.url ?? state.url`). Tapping tabs/menu/cancel on a reader-view page shows the internal localhost reader URL in the address bar. Fix: restore `currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL`.
findings.failureMode: In reader view, tap tabs/menu/cancel → address bar URL becomes http://localhost:6571/reader-mode/page?url=… instead of the article URL.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now keeps raw reader-mode localhost URL

findings.description: In Proactive posture, the Status select binds to `trigger.after` and nothing sets `trigger.expect`. The work-pool and work-queue siblings bind `expect` in both postures. Choosing Proactive + Not Ready produces `{posture: Proactive, after: ["prefect.deployment.not-ready"]}` with no `expect` (checked by running the component). The server's `expects()` returns True for any event when `expect` is empty, so the automation ignores the selected status and fires only if the deployment emits no event at all. Switching Reactive→Proactive also leaves the earlier `expect` value in place while the select appears empty. Fix: bind the status select to `trigger.expect` in both postures, as the work-pool and work-queue components do.
findings.failureMode: Proactive deployment-status automation is saved with wrong event criteria (after set, expect empty/stale) → fires/doesn't fire on the wrong events.
findings.title: Proactive deployment status written to `after` with empty `expect`

findings.description: `e.target.value.split("\n")` always returns ≥1 element, so the `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` fallback is dead code. Clearing the textarea stores `expect: [""]` instead of undefined, and a trailing newline stores `["prefect.x", ""]` (checked by running the component). On the server, `matches("", event)` compares `value == expected` and never matches, so a Reactive custom trigger saved with the textarea cleared never fires. Fix: filter out blank lines (`.filter((l) => l.trim() !== "")`) before the length check.
findings.failureMode: User clears events textarea (or leaves trailing newline) → trigger.expect contains "" → automation never fires / expects a non-existent event instead of 'any event'.
findings.title: Custom events keep blank lines; cleared textarea stores [""]

findings.description: The threshold onChange uses `parseInt(e.target.value)`, while the other four trigger components use `Number(...)`. Clearing the input stores `NaN` in `trigger.threshold` (checked by running the component), and zod then rejects it with 'Expected number, received nan'. Inputs such as `1e3` are truncated to 1. Fix: use `Number(e.target.value)` like the sibling components.
findings.failureMode: Empty/exponent/decimal threshold input yields NaN or a truncated threshold in the work-pool status trigger only.
findings.title: Work-pool threshold uses parseInt, diverging from siblings

findings.description: The new condition `'$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'` runs the servicing reference-change check only on patch 1 and turns it off for every later patch. Patch 1 is exactly when the baseline is still stale: Baseline.Designer.props is still 9.0.0. The repo's existing patch-1 exemption uses `!= '1'` (Directory.Build.targets.in). This PR makes IsServicingBuild true with patch 1, so BUILD002 now fires on stale 9.0 baselines. Example: the 9.0.0 baseline for Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup (net10.0 condition) lists System.Text.Json, but the 10.0 csproj no longer references it, so the build fails with "Package references changed since the last release". From 10.0.2 on, the guard is permanently off. Fix: use `!= '1'`.
findings.failureMode: The 10.0.1 servicing build fails with BUILD002 for HostingStartup; from 10.0.2 on, reference removals in servicing are no longer caught.
findings.title: BUILD002 patch-version guard inverted (== '1' instead of != '1')

findings.description: Loop changed from `j < numkeys` to `j <= numkeys`. On the last iteration it reads keys_result->keys[numkeys] (stale/uninitialized entry; pos 0 for keysbuf, garbage for heap) and writes slot_buffer[numkeys], one past a numkeys-sized malloc. For a single-key command like `SET foo bar` in cluster mode, keys[1].pos is 0 → hashes argv[0] "SET" → slot differs → CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT for nearly every keyed command; heap-allocated keys (>6 keys) give garbage pos → out-of-bounds argv read/crash; the buffer write is heap corruption. Fix: use `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Heap buffer overflow + spurious CROSSSLOT errors / crash for keyed commands in cluster mode
findings.title: Off-by-one `<=` reads keys[numkeys] and overflows slot_buffer

Also violates AGENTS.md rules 2 and 4. The buffer is never read; delete it, or use zmalloc/zfree.

Now testClipboard (TestRail 2325688) passes on iOS 15 without verifying anything about the clipboard. `checkCopiedUrl` is left as dead code; its only other reference is commented out. The PR only says it removes tests marked for deletion, and nothing in the diff replaces this check. Fix: restore the `checkCopiedUrl()` call.
findings.failureMode: On iOS 15 runs, a regression where Copy puts nothing (or the wrong URL) on the pasteboard is no longer caught, and testClipboard passes vacuously.
findings.title: testClipboard no longer checks the copied URL on iOS < 16

findings.description: `checkUrl` (line 11), `copyUrl` (line 17) and `checkCopiedUrl` (line 41) changed from internal `func` to `public func`. They are called only inside ClipBoardTests, as grep shows. AGENTS.md rule 11 says members must not be public when they are only used internally. Rule 14 says public APIs need `///` doc comments, but these have only `//` comments. Fix: revert them to internal or make them private.
findings.failureMode: Violates mandatory repository rules 11 (access control) and 14 (public API docs) at three changed sites. The test class's internal helpers are needlessly exposed as public API.
findings.title: Class-only helpers made public without /// docs

findings.description: `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets a missing or None `result` through, so `render_template` (declared `-> str`) can return None. CI runs `dev/basedpyright-check` in strict mode, and it fails with `template_renderer.py:40:16 - error: Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str"`. At runtime, a None result reaches `len(rendered)` in TemplateTransformNode._run and raises an uncaught TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult. Fix: `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)`.
findings.failureMode: Type-check CI failure (reportReturnType error). A None render result also crashes the node with a TypeError instead of producing a FAILED result.
findings.title: render_template can return None despite `-> str`; fails strict basedpyright

This breaks mandate 2 (`ruff check` must pass). Fix: `assert result.outputs["output"] == "1, two, 3.0, True"`.
findings.failureMode: `ruff check` fails with SIM300 on a changed line.
findings.title: Yoda-condition assert fails ruff check (SIM300)

Each fits on one 120-char line, so the formatter would collapse both. Fix: run `ruff format` to put each signature on one line.
findings.failureMode: `ruff format --check` fails on the changed test file, which violates the ruff mandate.
findings.title: New test signatures fail ruff format

findings.description: Loop bound changed from `j < keys_result->numkeys` to `j <= keys_result->numkeys`. The extra iteration reads `keys[numkeys]` (zeroed keysbuf entry -> pos 0 -> argv[0], the command name; or the `keys` pointer bytes when numkeys==6 -> argv[huge]) and writes one int past `slot_buffer`. Verified at runtime (malloc->zmalloc patched to get a build): single-node cluster with all slots, `SET foo bar` and `GET foo` both return CROSSSLOT; `DEL {a}1 ... {a}6` crashes the server in extractSlotFromKeysResult. Fix: restore `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Cluster mode: every keyed command (e.g. GET foo) rejected with CROSSSLOT; a 6-key command segfaults the server; heap overflow on slot_buffer; ASM feed sees CROSSSLOT and cancels migrations.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads keys[numkeys] and writes slot_buffer[numkeys]

findings.description: `malloc(sizeof(int) * keys_result->numkeys)` at cluster.c:1110. server.h marks malloc deprecated and src/Makefile WARN has `-Werror=deprecated-declarations`, so cluster.o fails to compile even with the default build; also violates AGENTS.md rule 2 (zmalloc) and rule 4 (-Werror clean). Fix: remove the unused slot_buffer, or use zmalloc.
findings.failureMode: `make` fails: cluster.c:1110:24: error: 'malloc' is deprecated [-Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations]; redis-server cannot be built.
findings.title: malloc() is deprecated in server.h: build fails (and violates zmalloc rule)

findings.failureMode: `make` fails: cluster.c:1120:13: error: 'free' is deprecated [-Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations].
findings.title: free() is deprecated in server.h: build fails (cross-slot path)

findings.description: `free(slot_buffer)` at cluster.c:1124 is a deprecated declaration under -Werror=deprecated-declarations (default WARN), so cluster.o fails to compile; also violates AGENTS.md rules 2 and 4. Fix: zfree (or drop the buffer).
findings.failureMode: `make` fails: cluster.c:1124:5: error: 'free' is deprecated [-Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations].

findings.description: @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") lets any team member (role MEMBER) pass RolesGuard, since hasMinimumRole accepts any role at or above the minimum. The PR requires TEAM_ADMIN, the sibling org invite controller uses TEAM_ADMIN, and the tRPC handler limits this to OWNER/ADMIN. A regular member can POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite, get a valid 7-day join token, and invite outsiders. The new e2e test expecting 403 for a MEMBER fails. Fix: @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: Authorization bypass: non-admin team members can mint team invite tokens/links.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows plain TEAM_MEMBER instead of TEAM_ADMIN

findings.description: This imports TeamService from "@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService". biome noRestrictedImports reports an error: API v2 may import only the platform-* packages and prisma. Also, api v2 does not depend on @calcom/features, and this is the only non-test src file importing it. The production build (tsc, then `node dist/.../main.js`) keeps the bare require, and node cannot resolve an extensionless path to a .ts-only file. That gives MODULE_NOT_FOUND when AppModule loads. The sibling controller imports TeamService from "@calcom/platform-libraries", which exports it. Fix: import from "@calcom/platform-libraries".
findings.failureMode: Lint error; API v2 production startup fails to resolve the module.
findings.title: API v2 imports @calcom/features directly (restricted, unbuilt TS)

findings.description: `token: newToken.identifier` returns the constant string `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` instead of the random token. The base code returned `token`. Every caller now gets the same value on every call (tRPC createInvite, the org invite endpoint and the new teams endpoint), and it does not match the token inside inviteLink. So the returned token can't be used to join. The existing org e2e test (not.toEqual(firstToken), inviteLink toContain token) and the new e2e test both fail. Fix: `token: newToken.token`, or just `token`.
findings.failureMode: Wrong output: returned token is a constant identifier, unusable and identical across invites.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of the token

findings.failureMode: Wrong invite link format for every team and organization invite.
findings.title: buildInviteLink condition inverted

findings.description: Changes `"strict": true` to `"strict": false` in tsconfig.app.json, which violates AGENTS.md rule 11 and removes strict checking for all of ui-v2/src. findings.title: Strict TypeScript checking disabled for ui-v2 app

findings.description: The work-pool threshold `onChange` uses the global `parseInt(e.target.value)`, while every parallel threshold/within input uses `Number(...)`. Biome flags this line as an error (lint/style/useNumberNamespace; it also warns useParseIntRadix), so the required `biome ci` step in ui-v2-checks Lint fails. At runtime, clearing the field stores NaN, because parseInt("") returns NaN where Number("") returns 0. The controlled input then receives value NaN, and zod reports "Expected number, received nan". Input like "1e3" is also truncated to 1. Fix: use `Number(e.target.value)` like the other components.
findings.failureMode: Lint CI job fails on biome error; cleared threshold stores NaN.
findings.title: parseInt on work-pool threshold fails biome ci and yields NaN

findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields binds Status to `trigger.expect` for every posture. WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields does the same at work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36. In contrast, the Deployment and FlowRunState fields switch to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive. A Proactive trigger fires when the expected events are absent. So choosing "Stays in" + "Paused" produces a trigger that fires when the pool/queue does NOT emit a paused event, which is the opposite of what the user asked for. Fix: bind to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive, as the deployment component does.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-pool/work-queue automations have inverted semantics and fire on the wrong condition.
findings.title: Proactive work-pool/queue status is stored in expect, not after

findings.description: `e.target.value.split("\n")` always returns at least one element, so `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` never yields undefined, and blank entries are never removed. Clearing the textarea stores `expect: [""]` instead of undefined, and a trailing newline adds "" (for example `["a", ""]`). The trigger then expects an event named "", so a cleared custom trigger that should match any event matches none. Fix: drop blank lines (`line.trim() !== ""`) before storing, so empty input becomes undefined. To still allow typing newlines, keep the raw text in local state.
findings.failureMode: Cleared or blank-line textarea submits expect [""]; trigger never matches events.
findings.title: Custom expect keeps blank lines; undefined branch is dead

findings.description: Pools moved to macOS-15 (lines 106, 322) and the step is relabelled "Use XCode 16.4.0" (lines 167, 393), but the script at lines 166/392 still runs `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer`. macOS-15 hosted images ship only Xcode 16.x, so xcode-select exits non-zero ("invalid developer directory") and every macOS job (ci.yml, ci-public.yml, quarantined-pr.yml) fails before building. findings.failureMode: macOS CI jobs fail at the xcode-select step on the macOS-15 image.

findings.failureMode: From 10.0.2 on, servicing builds no longer fail when a package reference is removed; in 10.0.1 the check runs against the stale 9.0.0 baseline.

EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes `schedule.data` (now this type) to `useAvailableTimeSlots({ schedule })`, which expects `IGetAvailableSlots`. findings.description: The removed trpc `Slot` declared `userIds?: number[];`, and the slot producer passes through numeric user IDs (`userIds?: number[]` in slots/util.ts). The moved copy declares `userIds?: string[]`. This type backs the public `onTimeslotsLoaded` callback and the getSchedule test matcher. Fix: declare `userIds?: number[]` to keep the moved type identical.

Running biome 2.3.10 `format` on the file reports a formatting error that rewrites all four lines to double quotes. Fix: run biome format on the file.

AGENTS.md rule 10 lists "Code throws generic Error objects" as a failure criterion; errors must extend a base type (HttpError / ErrorWithCode) with a typed code and status. findings.failureMode: Callers get an uncategorized Error with no code or status, so they can't tell a validation failure apart from other failures or map it to a 400.
findings.title: New validator throws generic Error, violating typed-error mandate

BVC maps `.readerModeLongPressAction` to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()` (add page to reading list) instead of `toggleReaderMode()`. Tapping the toolbar reader-mode button, the summarizer long-press, or VoiceOver magic tap (all dispatch showReaderMode) no longer enters/exits reader view; it adds the page to the reading list. `.readerMode` display is now never produced. Fix: restore `displayView: .readerMode`.

Every reader-mode tap now records the opposite state. With the unchanged extras mapping, the existing test testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes (readerModeState nil, expects isPrivate == false) now gets isPrivate == true and fails. Reader-mode URLs are `http://localhost:PORT/reader-mode/page?url=...`, which isWebPage() already accepts, so the exclusion is gone. On a reader-mode tab, tapping tabs/menu/cancel dispatches cancelEdit with the raw localhost URL; AddressBarState uses `toolbarAction.url ?? state.url`, overwriting the decoded displayURL that BVC normally sets. Fix: restore `currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL`.
findings.failureMode: In reader view, tap menu or tabs button → address bar shows http://localhost:6571/reader-mode/page?url=... instead of the article URL.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now leaks internal reader-mode URL into address bar

findings.description: `private let gleanWrapper` became `let gleanWrapper` (internal). Nothing reads it outside the struct, so this only exposes an implementation detail. AGENTS.md rule 11 requires `private` for implementation details. Fix: restore `private`.
findings.failureMode: Any module code can now reach the telemetry wrapper and record events, bypassing ToolbarTelemetry's API. Violates the access-control mandate.
findings.title: gleanWrapper access widened from private to internal

findings.description: Base called `onboardingService.handleAction(...)` synchronously inside the @MainActor `onActionTap` closure. Head wraps it in `Task { }`, so the action, and the completion that advances `pageCount`, now runs on a later main-actor turn, after `onActionTap` has returned. OnboardingViewCompact.handleBottomButtonAction posts `UIAccessibility.post(.screenChanged)` right after `viewModel.handleBottomButtonAction` returns on forward actions, so that notification now fires before the page changes. The Task also keeps a strong reference to the service, so a queued action can still run after onDismiss/onComplete has set `onboardingService = nil`. The closure is already main-actor isolated, so the Task is not needed. Fix: remove the `Task` and call handleAction synchronously, as base did.
findings.failureMode: A forward-button tap in compact onboarding posts VoiceOver `.screenChanged` before `pageCount` advances, so focus/announcement can land on the outgoing card. A queued action can also run on an orphaned service after the flow is dismissed.
findings.title: Onboarding action handling deferred into unstructured Task

findings.description: The diff deletes `struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }` and replaces `UX.buttonSize` with literal `40` in both close-button constraints, violating AGENTS.md rule 13 (UI constants must live in a nested UX struct).
findings.failureMode: Mandated UX-struct convention broken: button size now duplicated as scattered literals; changing one site without the other yields a non-square button.

findings.description: WorkflowRun.inputs and outputs are saved with plain json.dumps, whose default ensure_ascii=True turns 中文 into `\u4e2d\u6587`. The deleted line `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` changed the keyword into that escaped form. The new code only runs escape_like_pattern on the raw keyword, so the pattern `%中文%` never matches the stored text. Fix: unicode-escape the keyword first, then call escape_like_pattern, e.g. `escape_like_pattern(keyword[:30].encode("unicode_escape").decode("utf-8"))`.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow app logs with a Chinese or other non-ASCII keyword returns zero input/output matches.
findings.title: Non-ASCII workflow log keyword search no longer matches

findings.description: escape_like_pattern prefixes %, _ and \ with a backslash, but the IRIS query declares `ESCAPE '|'`. Backslash is then a literal char and %/_ stay wildcards. Query "test_data" becomes `%test\_data%`, which needs a literal backslash, so a text containing "test_data" no longer matches (the base code did match). "50%" becomes `%50\%%` and misses "50% off". A query containing `|` is now read as an escape sequence. Fix: use `ESCAPE '\'` so it matches the helper.
findings.failureMode: Full-text LIKE fallback (IRIS_TEXT_INDEX=false) returns no documents for queries containing _, % or \ that matched before.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE uses ESCAPE '|' but pattern escaped with backslash

findings.description: "not contains" escapes the value with backslashes but calls `notlike` with no `escape="\\"`. The sibling cases (contains, start with, end with) pass it. The helper documents that its output needs `ESCAPE '\'`. Without the clause the result depends on the database's default escape character. MySQL, for example, uses no escape character when NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES is set. In that case "not contains 50%" becomes `%50\%%`, excludes only text containing "50\", and keeps documents containing "50%". Fix: add `escape="\\"` to the notlike call.
findings.failureMode: Metadata "not contains" filter with %/_ in the value fails to exclude matching documents on DBs whose LIKE default escape is not backslash.
findings.title: "not contains" filter escapes value but omits escape clause

findings.description: The new local `escapedPattern` uses camelCase. AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule 16 requires snake_case for Python variables. Rename it to `escaped_pattern`, or return the expression directly.
findings.failureMode: Breaks mandatory repository naming rule 16.
findings.title: camelCase local variable breaks snake_case mandate

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, but prepare_tools returns crate::Result and applies `?` at lines 232, 239, 245, 251, 259. crate::Error has From<io::Error>/From<anyhow::Error> but no From<FileWriteError>, so `?` fails with E0277 on every Linux build of tauri-bundler (and tauri-cli, which depends on it). Fix: return std::io::Result<()> as before, or add a From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error variant.
findings.failureMode: Compilation error E0277 (`?` couldn't convert the error to `crate::Error`) when building tauri-bundler for target_os = linux.
findings.title: FileWriteError not convertible to crate::Error: Linux build fails

findings.description: Base wrote first then chmod'd (`fs::write(path, data)?; fs::set_permissions(...)?;`). The new code calls fs::set_permissions before fs::write. All callers except gtk only call it when `!path.exists()`, so set_permissions hits ENOENT and returns an error. This breaks the AppRun, linuxdeploy, gstreamer plugin, and even the "optional" appimage plugin download (its error propagates with `?`). On a clean tools cache, AppImage bundling always fails. Fix: restore the order: write the file, then set 0o770.
findings.failureMode: On first run (empty ~/.cache/tauri), prepare_tools errors with "Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory" and AppImage bundling aborts.
findings.title: set_permissions runs before file exists; every fresh tool write fails

findings.description: Base used `if !gtk.exists()`; the diff changed it to `if gtk.exists()`. When linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is missing from the tools dir (a fresh machine or cleared cache), the embedded script is never written. linuxdeploy is always run with `--plugin gtk`, so it cannot find the plugin and bundling fails. When the file does exist, it is rewritten on every run for no reason. Fix: restore `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: A new user runs `tauri build` for an AppImage, and linuxdeploy fails because the gtk plugin script was never created.
findings.title: Inverted gtk.exists() check: GTK plugin never written on fresh cache

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 says custom error enums must use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes. The new FileWriteError implements Display and Error by hand, even though thiserror is already a dependency. The manual `write!(f, "...: {}", e)` bodies also use non-inlined format args, which trip clippy's uninlined_format_args under the rule-2 `-D warnings` gate. Fix: derive thiserror::Error with #[error("Failed to write file: {0}")] etc., or drop the type entirely.
findings.failureMode: Violates mandatory rule 8 (thiserror for custom errors). The manual format strings can also fail the clippy -D warnings gate.
findings.title: FileWriteError hand-implements Display/Error instead of thiserror

findings.description: The new condition skips `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Light")` for every OnboardingTests test on iPad, not just the skipped testSelectBottomPlacement. testFirstRunTourDarkMode has no iPad guard and calls `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Dark")`, so the comment "theme is not changed there" is wrong. The theme is stored in UserDefaults.standard (`prefKeyThemeName`), and ClearProfile/resetApplication only clears the documents dir, caches and cookies. So Dark mode now stays on for every later test on the same iPad simulator. Fix: drop `|| iPad()` and gate only on the test that is skipped.
findings.failureMode: On iPad with iOS 17+, testFirstRunTourDarkMode sets Dark and tearDown returns early without resetting it. Later tests (FullFunctionalTestPlan does not skip these) then run in Dark theme.
findings.title: `|| iPad()` stops the Light theme reset for every iPad test

findings.description: `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` is renamed to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`. XCTest only discovers methods whose names start with `test`, so TestRail case 2864380 silently stops running, including in FullFunctionalTestPlan, which does not skip ShareLongPressTests. This also breaks mandate #6 (test methods must start with 'test'). AccessibilityTestPlan still lists the old name `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`, which is now stale. Fix: keep the `test` prefix and disable the test through a test-plan skip or XCTSkip.
findings.failureMode: Bookmark → Share → Reminders is no longer tested in any plan, and the result does not show up as skipped.
findings.title: Renamed test lacks `test` prefix, so XCTest never runs it

findings.description: The new `return` exits tearDown before `app.terminate()` and `try await super.tearDown()`. This happens for testSelectBottomPlacement on every device and for every OnboardingTests test on iPad. In the base code, only the theme switch was conditional (on iOS 17). Now the app keeps running after the test and BaseTestCase/XCTestCase teardown never runs. Fix: skip only the theme switch and fall through to terminate and super.tearDown.
findings.failureMode: After testSelectBottomPlacement, or any iPad onboarding test on iOS 17+, the app is left running and the superclass teardown never runs. Teardown behaviour is lost for these tests.
findings.title: Early `return` skips `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`

findings.description: The press was shortened from 1.0s to 0.5s. BookmarksViewController uses a default UILongPressGestureRecognizer, whose minimum press duration is also 0.5s. Every other context-menu long press in the suite uses 1.0s or more. At exactly the threshold, lifting the touch can win the race, so the table treats it as a tap and opens the bookmark. That dismisses the library, and pressWithRetry's retries then target a cell that no longer exists, so the test fails. Fix: use a duration safely above 0.5s, such as 1.0–1.5s.
findings.failureMode: If the touch lifts before the recognizer fires, the bookmark opens instead of the context menu. The retry cannot recover, so the bookmark share tests fail intermittently.
findings.title: 0.5s press equals the long-press threshold and can register as a tap

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc=6 but receives 7 objects (hsetex, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj). The function reads only argc va_args, so newobj is dropped and the propagated command is `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field` with no value. HSETEX parsing rejects it on replicas and during AOF load, so the incremented value never reaches replicas or the AOF. Increments are lost after an AOF restart, and replicas keep the old value. The new test's stream assertion `{hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *}` also fails. Fix: pass argc 7.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT propagates a malformed HSETEX with no value. Replicas and AOF replay reject it, so the value update is lost and data diverges.
findings.title: argc 6 drops the value from the replicated HSETEX

findings.description: The base called `hashTypeSet(..., HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL)`. The new line passes only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE. Without that flag, hashTypeSet calls listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL) or hfieldPersist on an existing field. So `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1` on a field with a TTL now makes the field persistent on the master. The replica receives HSETEX KEEPTTL and keeps the TTL, which reverses the inconsistency this PR set out to fix. The field never expires on the master. Fix: restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with a TTL removes the TTL on the master while the replica keeps it, so the master and replica diverge.
findings.title: HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL removed: master now drops field TTL

findings.description: The base declared `static GetFieldRes addHashFieldToReply(...)`. The diff removes `static`, but every caller is in t_hash.c and no header declares the function. This breaks AGENTS.md rule 7 (internal helpers must be static) and exports an unneeded symbol.
findings.failureMode: The single-file helper is now exported as a global symbol, which breaks the static-helper mandate.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply lost its static keyword

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>. prepare_tools returns crate::Result and applies `?` at lines 232, 239, 245, 251 and 259. crate::Error has `#[from]` conversions for io::Error, anyhow::Error and others, but none for FileWriteError, and `?` does not chain conversions through anyhow. The result is E0277 when building on Linux, where the linux module is compiled, which breaks the tauri-bundler/CLI build and clippy CI. Fix: return std::io::Result<()> again, or add a `#[from]` variant to crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: `cargo build` on Linux fails with E0277: `?` couldn't convert the error from FileWriteError to crate::Error.
findings.title: FileWriteError has no From impl into crate::Error; `?` fails to compile

findings.description: Base wrote the plugin when `!gtk.exists()`; head writes it only when it already exists. On a fresh tools dir (first build, CI), linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never created, yet the command always passes `--plugin gtk`, so linuxdeploy fails to find the plugin and AppImage bundling fails. Fix: `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: Fresh cache: `--plugin gtk` points to a missing script, so linuxdeploy exits with an error and no AppImage is produced.
findings.title: Inverted gtk.exists() check: GTK plugin never written on fresh cache

findings.description: Base wrote the file first and then chmod'ed it (`fs::write(path, data)?; fs::set_permissions(...)`). Head calls `fs::set_permissions` first. Every caller runs only when the file is missing (`!apprun.exists()`, `!linuxdeploy.exists()`, `!gstreamer.exists()`, `!appimage.exists()`), so chmod on a missing path returns NotFound. That error is returned before anything is written, so on a fresh cache every tool download fails and bundling aborts. Fix: restore the order, write first and then set permissions.
findings.failureMode: First AppImage build: prepare_tools downloads AppRun, and write_and_make_executable returns Permissions(NotFound), so the bundle fails.
findings.title: set_permissions before write fails with ENOENT for new files

findings.description: The new `fs::set_permissions(...).map_err(FileWriteError::Permissions)?;` line is 101 columns, over rustfmt.toml's max_width = 100. rustfmt would move `.map_err(...)` to its own line, so the required fmt workflow (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`) fails, violating mandate 3. findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes. FileWriteError adds hand-written `impl std::fmt::Display` and `impl std::error::Error`, which the rule names as its failure criterion. thiserror is already a dependency of this crate (error.rs). Fix: derive thiserror::Error with #[error("Failed to write file: {0}")] / #[error("Failed to set permissions: {0}")] and #[source].

findings.description: `rewriteClientCommandVector(c, 6, shared.hsetex, c->argv[1], shared.keepttl, shared.fields, shared.integers[1], c->argv[2], newobj)` passes 7 objects but argc=6, so the value (newobj) is dropped. The propagated command is `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field`, which fails the arity check. Confirmed by execution: the AOF contains a 6-arg HSETEX with no value, and on reload the field is still `1` instead of `2.1` with 'wrong number of arguments for hsetex' logged. Fix: pass argc 7.
findings.failureMode: Every HINCRBYFLOAT is propagated as a malformed HSETEX: replicas error (ignored by default → silent divergence, or panic if propagation-error-behavior=panic) and AOF reload loses every HINCRBYFLOAT update (data loss).
findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector argc 6 drops value

findings.description: The diff removed HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL from the master-side hashTypeSet call (base: `hashTypeSet(...,new,HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL);`). Without that flag, hashTypeSet persists the field, so HINCRBYFLOAT removes the field's TTL on the master. Confirmed by execution: after `hsetex h1 EX 100 ... f1 1; hincrbyfloat h1 f1 1.1`, the master reports `httl` = -1. The replica/AOF gets HSETEX KEEPTTL and keeps the TTL, so the divergence is reversed rather than fixed. The new test checks TTL only on the replica, so it misses this. Fix: restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: hsetex h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1; hincrbyfloat h1 f1 1.1 → master httl f1 = -1 (TTL lost), replica httl f1 ≈ 100. Data inconsistency between master and replica; field that should expire never does on master.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT now drops field TTL on master

findings.description: Base had `static GetFieldRes addHashFieldToReply(...)`; diff drops `static`. Fix: restore `static`.
findings.failureMode: Internal helper becomes an externally-visible symbol in the redis-server link unit, violating mandated encapsulation rule 7; risk of symbol collision with other compilation units.

Callers such as android_studio_script.rs then read `build.dev_url` from the unmerged config.

findings.title: `&&` makes schema-validation condition unsatisfiable

findings.description: The base code converted the keyword with `.encode('unicode_escape')` and rewrote `\u` as `\\u` (removed line: `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")`). That conversion was needed because WorkflowRun.inputs and outputs are stored with plain `json.dumps` (ensure_ascii=True), so non-ASCII text is saved as `\u4f60\u597d`. The new code passes the raw keyword to escape_like_pattern. A search for "你好" now builds `%你好%`, which never matches the stored `\u4f60\u597d`, so the result is an empty log list. Fix: apply unicode_escape to the trimmed keyword before calling escape_like_pattern. The helper then doubles the backslash, which matches a literal `\u` under ESCAPE '\'.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow app logs by any non-ASCII keyword (e.g. Chinese) returns no matches on inputs/outputs, regression from base
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search drops unicode_escape; non-ASCII keywords stop matching

findings.description: escape_like_pattern prefixes %, _ and \ with a backslash, but the IRIS LIKE fallback declares `ESCAPE '|'`. With '|' as the escape char, the backslash is literal and the following % or _ is still a wildcard. A query of "50%" becomes `%50\%%`, which needs a literal "50\" in the text, so "50% discount" no longer matches. Any query that contains %, _ or \ returns no or wrong results. Fix: use `ESCAPE '\'` so the clause matches the helper.
findings.failureMode: Full-text LIKE fallback returns no results for queries containing %, _ or \ (regression vs base which matched them)
findings.title: IRIS LIKE uses ESCAPE '|' but pattern escaped with backslash

Fix: pass `escape="\\"` to notlike.

findings.title: "not contains" escapes value but omits escape="\\" on notlike

findings.description: The guard `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets a missing or None `result` through, so `render_template` returns `str | None` even though it is annotated `-> str`.
